name: Greek Butter Cookies with Almonds & Powdered Sugar (Kourabiedes)

instructions.primary_message: Cut butter into small pieces. Place in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, then set aside to soften.
Place flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dry ingredients and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 ½ tsp baking powder
¼ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Transfer almonds to a large baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and toast, stirring almonds halfway through, until lightly toasted, about 5 minutes. Remove from oven and let cool completely, 5-10 minutes.

Once the almonds are completely cool, transfer to a food processor. Pulse on low until the nuts are coarsely chopped, about 30 seconds (alternatively, you can mince them using a chef's knife). Add to the bowl with the dry ingredients and set aside. (Reserve baking sheet for later use.)

Working over a small bowl, separate egg yolks from whites, leaving the whites in the bowl. Place yolks in another small bowl, along with vanilla, then whisk to combine the wet ingredients. Set aside. (Reserve egg whites for another use.)
Once the butter has softened, beat on medium-high speed until light and creamy, 2-3 minutes. Stop the mixer and scrape down the sides of the bowl with a silicone spatula.

Add sugar to the mixer (pressing it through a strainer, if necessary, to remove any lumps). Continue mixing on medium speed until the butter mixture is light in color and fluffy in texture, 3-5 minutes more. Stop the mixer and scrape down the sides of the bowl.
Add egg yolk-vanilla mixture to the bowl with the butter mixture. Mix on medium speed until fully combined. Scrape down the sides of the bowl.
Add dry ingredients and chopped almonds to the bowl. Mix on low speed until dough is just combined. Remove bowl from mixer.
Line the reserved baking sheet and one additional baking sheet with parchment paper.

Using a 2 tbsp cookie scoop, portion the dough and roll into round balls using your hands. Arrange balls on the baking sheets, spacing them about 1-inch apart, then gently press down on the dough with your fingers (the cookies should retain most of their round shape while having a slightly flattened top and bottom). Alternatively, the cookies can be formed into a crescent moon shape.

Place cookies in the oven and bake, rotating baking sheets halfway through, until golden brown at the edges and firm to the touch, 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, using the strainer, sift additional sugar into a clean medium bowl.

Once the cookies have cooled slightly, gently lift away from the parchment. Working with a few cookies at a time, add to the bowl with the powdered sugar and gently turn to coat. Return to the baking sheets and set aside to cool completely, about 20 minutes.
Arrange cookies on a serving platter and dust with more powdered sugar, if desired. Enjoy!
